name: 🛡️ Zero-Leak AI Customer Support: Auto-Triage & Reply with PII Guardrails

parameters.content:
## 🛡️ Zero-Leak AI Customer Support: Auto-Triage & Reply with PII Guardrails

### How it works

This workflow accepts a customer support ticket either from a manual test trigger or an inbound webhook, then normalizes the ticket fields into a consistent payload. It masks personally identifiable information before sending the sanitized ticket to OpenAI for triage and draft reply generation. After the AI response is produced, it restores the protected data and formats the final CRM dispatch and audit trail payload.

### Setup steps

- Configure the webhook URL and ensure inbound ticket requests include the expected fields such as ticket ID, channel, customer name, customer email, subject, and message content.
- Set up credentials or configuration for the Enterprise PII Guardrails nodes so masking and restoration share the same protection context.
- Configure the OpenAI node with a valid API credential, model choice, and prompt instructions for support triage and response drafting.
- Review the final Set node fields to match the schema expected by your CRM, helpdesk, or downstream audit logging system.

### Customization

Adjust the ticket payload fields, PII masking policy, OpenAI prompt, triage categories, and final CRM output fields to match your support process and compliance requirements.

## Inbound ticket intake

Receives test or live customer support tickets and standardizes the incoming data into a customer ticket payload.

## Mask sensitive data

Applies PII guardrails to redact or tokenize sensitive customer information before the ticket content is sent to the AI model.

## AI triage drafting

Uses OpenAI to classify or triage the sanitized support request and draft an appropriate customer support response.

## Restore and format output

Restores protected PII after AI processing and formats the final ticket response, CRM dispatch fields, and audit trail payload.

values.content:
You are an enterprise AI customer support triage and resolution assistant for a healthcare & billing platform.

TASK:
1. Analyze the customer's incoming ticket.
2. Determine:
   - Priority: High / Medium / Low
   - Category: Billing Dispute / Prescription Claim / General Inquiry
   - Sentiment: Frustrated / Neutral / Satisfied
3. Draft a professional, empathetic, and comprehensive resolution email acknowledging the issue, confirming that the overcharge adjustment is initiated, and outlining the next steps.

CRITICAL PRIVACY & TOKEN RECONSTRUCTION RULES:
The incoming ticket has been sanitized by Enterprise PII Guardrails with surrogate tokens enclosed in angle brackets (e.g. <PERSON_...>, <EMAIL_...>, <PHONE_...>, <BANK_ACCOUNT_...>, <MEDICAL_RECORD_...>, <CREDIT_CARD_...>, <CREDIT_CARD_EXPIRY_...>, <STREET_ADDRESS_...>, <LOCATION_...>, <SSN_...>).
Our automated core CRM router requires exact verbatim token matching to unmask and restore customer details upon dispatch. You MUST:
1. Greet the customer using their exact surrogate person token from the ticket (e.g., "Dear <PERSON_...>,") - copy the entire token verbatim including brackets and any inner hint text. Never omit or shorten any token!
2. Specifically acknowledge the dispute using the exact surrogate tokens from the ticket for their card, expiry date, and patient record.
3. State clearly that the refund for the $275 difference will be credited back to the customer's card token and the receipt sent to their email token verbatim.
4. Include a structured "Ticket Triage Summary" header at the top of the email:
   - Priority: [High / Medium / Low]
   - Category: [Billing Dispute / Pharmacy Claims]
   - Sentiment: [Customer Sentiment]
5. STRICT VERBATIM PRESERVATION: Never strip, truncate, or alter surrogate tokens. If a token in the ticket is `<PERSON_1:AXXX...>` or `<EMAIL_1:aXXX...>`, you MUST preserve the entire string `<...>` exactly as written in the ticket. Do NOT shorten to `<PERSON_1>` or `<EMAIL_1>`.
